title: Performance Microcards Lattice: compact token + cost stitching for model & route views
creator: Ava Kim
description: Design a compact, scannable grid of performance microcards (the 'Lattice') that surfaces per-model and per-route KPIs — p50/p95 latency, tokens/request, requests/sec, error rate, and cost-per-1k-tokens — with inline sparkline, small waterfall preview, and a lightweight drill path into the full route/mode dashboard. Focus: maximize information density for SREs and product owners while keeping interactions mobile-friendly and accessible.
background: Current per-route dashboards are full-page charts and long tables. Customers told us they want a condensed overview for on-call rotation pages and executive summaries. This ticket explores a microcard lattice that can be embedded in consoles, project overviews, and rollout pages. We need consistent chart specs across model vs route contexts and a predictable cost stitching model for mixed-model route fallbacks.
design_goals: Scannability: users should identify hotspots (latency / cost) at a glance within 2 seconds
Compactness: each card <= 160px tall and fits 3 columns at medium breakpoint
Drillability: tap/click opens unified detail panel (left slide-over) rather than navigating away
Consistency: same color and thresholds across console so latency P95 looks identical everywhere
Cost stitching: show amortized cost-per-1k-tokens combining generation + embedding tokens and routing fallbacks
acceptance_criteria: Visual comps for desktop (3 cols), tablet (2 cols), mobile (single column) approved
Prototype demonstrates hover tooltips, click-to-open detail slide-over, and keyboard focus state
Chart specs included (sparkline sampling, waterfall microtraces, stacked area for throughput) with data contract for backend
Design handoff includes color tokens, typography scales, and spacing utility values
PM and Eng have signed off on cost-stitching definition and API shape
chart_specs: Sparkline: 120x28 px, 1px stroke, adaptive sampling at 60 points, antialiasing off, color variable --redwood-ink-700 for latency increases
Mini-waterfall: 120x36 px, stacked segments representing request phases (decode, kv-hit, compute, postproc), hover reveals milliseconds per phase and sample trace link
Throughput strip: micro-bar of 12 columns representing requests/sec buckets over rolling 1h window, highlight current bucket
Stacked-cost area (hidden by default): 120x28 px, two layers (generation tokens / embedding tokens), legend collapsed into tooltip
Threshold overlay: optional 95th percentile line in muted dashed stroke; color becomes accent if exceeded
data_contract_notes: Response fields required: p50_ms, p95_ms, requests_per_min, avg_tokens_per_request, tokens_generated, tokens_embedded, cost_per_1k_tokens_cents, error_rate, sample_trace_id
Fallbacks: when route has multiple model variants, API must return weighted averages and top-3 variant breakdowns
Missing data policy: show -- for metrics with <5 samples, greyed sparkline and tooltip: 'insufficient data'
ux_flow_summary: User arrives at project Overview -> microcard lattice shows top 12 routes (sorted by cost impact). Click a card to open slide-over with 1) expanded charts, 2) recent traces, 3) quick actions (pin route, create alert, open rollout). Hover reveals tooltip with p50/p95 and cost delta vs baseline. Keyboard 'Enter' on focused card opens slide-over.
interactions: Hover: show compact tooltip with last-1h summary
Click: open slide-over anchored to lattice with deep links to route page
Keyboard: Tab-able cards, Enter to open, Escape to close slide-over
Context menu (right click): quick actions (Mute alerts, Open traces, Open rollout)
accessibility_notes: All metrics must have aria-labels with human-readable summaries (e.g., 'P95 latency 320 milliseconds, up 18% vs baseline'),
Color contrast: use >=4.5:1 for text; sparklines have sufficient contrast in hover state
Reduce motion: sparklines static when prefers-reduced-motion is set
decisions: Use slide-over for detail to avoid full navigation and maintain context
Default sorting: cost impact descending, fallback to p95 latency for ties
Show cost-per-1k-tokens on microcard primary line; full cost breakdown in slide-over
Expose top-3 model variant contributions when route has dynamic routing
tradeoffs: Density vs legibility: limited pixels force fewer labels; we surface precise values on hover/slide-over
Backend complexity: cost stitching requires additional aggregation in stat pipeline; increases latency of microcard API by ~50ms (acceptable for overview use-case)
Mobile limitations: waterfall microtrace collapses to a single-phase indicator on small screens
feedback: PM - Lina O'Connor: prefer callout for anything >30% cost regression; ensure alert creation is 2-click flow
Eng - Daniel Park: clarify data contract for weighted averages; request sample size field to avoid misleading p95 when sparse
SRE - Jon Matthews: make error-rate badge color-coded and machine-readable for pager integrations
Design review - Priya Sharma: microcard padding should follow 8px grid; recommend 12px internal gutters for touch targets
risks: Overloading overview pages with too many dense microcards may increase cognitive load for new users
Cost-stitching accuracy depends on timely token attribution from router; if router lag exists, numbers may be stale
Backend aggregation costs could increase OLAP bill if naive materialization is used
mitigations: Introduce 'summary mode' toggle that collapses microcards to bare minimum metrics for first-time users
Add 'data last updated' timestamp and sample_count on each card tooltip
Prototype with streaming metrics endpoint (SSE) disabled by default; start with 1m resolution, then optimize
handoff_files: Figma frames: 'Lattice / Desktop', 'Lattice / Tablet', 'Slide-over Detail', 'Mobile Collapse'
engineering_notes: Implement initial rendering server-side with skeleton cards to avoid layout shift
Cache microcard responses for 15s; background refresh for live update
Backfill sample_trace_id links to trace viewer at /traces/{id}
next_steps: Address Eng feedback on sample-size field and update API contract
Create responsive dev tickets (ENG-xxxx) for lattice frontend implementation
Run usability test with 6 SREs to validate scannability hypothesis
Finalize color tokens and produce token mapping for theme variables
